hook.line: Telling a story is a juggling act: what happened, what the scene looked like, and what had already happened before. Don Hernando always does it in that order.
hook.es: Era domingo. Tomás abrió la caja que había encontrado y vio una carta.
hook.en: It was Sunday. Tomás opened the box he had found and saw a letter.

examples.en: It was Sunday and it was raining.

examples.es: Tomás abrió la caja que había encontrado y vio una carta.
examples.en: Tomás opened the box he had found and saw a letter.

examples.es: Hacía frío y llovía cuando salimos del café.
examples.en: It was cold and raining when we left the café.

examples.es: Cuando llegué, Vale ya había salido.
examples.en: When I arrived, Vale had already left.

examples.es: Tomás estaba leyendo cuando sonó el celular.
examples.en: Tomás was reading when the cell phone rang.

examples.es: Entró Hernando, se sentó y pidió un tinto.
examples.en: Hernando came in, sat down and ordered a black coffee.

rule:
A story uses three pasts, each with a job.

The simple past (*abrió*, *vio*, *entró*) is the events, one after another. The story moves.

The imperfect (*era*, *llovía*, *hacía frío*, *estaba leyendo*) is the background: time, weather, what was going on. The story waits.

*Había* plus the *-ado* or *-ido* form (*había encontrado*, *había salido*) steps back to something that happened before the story's own starting point.

When an event breaks into the background, it gets the simple past: *Estaba leyendo cuando sonó el celular.*

For each verb, ask: is it moving the story, painting the scene, or stepping back?
smallPrint: Teachers call the events the foreground and the scene the background. The three tenses are the preterite, the imperfect and the pluperfect.

readAndPick.es: Tomás estaba leyendo cuando sonó el celular.
options: Tomás was reading when the cell phone rang.
Tomás read the letter when the cell phone rang.
Tomás had read when the cell phone rang.

readAndPick.es: Cuando llegué, Vale ya había salido.
options: When I arrived, Vale left.
When I arrived, Vale was leaving.
When I arrived, Vale had already left.
It was Sunday and it was raining.
It became Sunday and it started raining.

readAndPick.es: Entró Hernando, se sentó y pidió un tinto.
options: Hernando used to sit down and order a black coffee.
Hernando came in, sat down and ordered a black coffee.

readAndPick.es: Rosa había escrito la carta años antes.
options: Rosa wrote the letter years earlier.
Rosa was writing the letter years earlier.
Rosa had written the letter years earlier.
While Tomás was reading, Simón was singing.
Tomás read, then Simón sang.

readAndPick.es: Cuando abrí la caja, vi las cartas.
options: When I opened the box, I saw the letters.
When I was opening the box, I had seen the letters.

readAndPick.es: Tomás nunca había visto esa foto.
options: Tomás never saw that photo.
Tomás had never seen that photo.

readAndPick.es: Joaquín ya se había ido cuando Rosa llegó.
options: Joaquín left when Rosa arrived.
Joaquín was leaving when Rosa arrived.
Joaquín had already left when Rosa arrived.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Cuando llegué, Vale ya ___.* (*salió* or *había salido*) When I arrived, Vale had already left.
yourTurn.answer: Cuando llegué, Vale ya había salido.
yourTurn.why: He left before you arrived, so step back with *había*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Tomás ___ leyendo cuando sonó el celular.* (*estaba* or *estuvo*) Tomás was reading when the cell phone rang.
yourTurn.answer: Tomás estaba leyendo cuando sonó el celular.
yourTurn.why: Reading is the background, so it takes the imperfect.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: It was Sunday and it was raining.
yourTurn.why: Day and weather set the scene, so both are in the imperfect.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Hernando came in, sat down and ordered a black coffee.
yourTurn.answer: Entró Hernando, se sentó y pidió un tinto.
accept: Hernando entró, se sentó y pidió un tinto.
yourTurn.why: Three events in a row are all in the simple past.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Tomás had never seen that photo.
yourTurn.answer: Tomás nunca había visto esa foto.
yourTurn.why: Before the story's starting point, so *había* plus *visto*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: It was cold and raining when we left the café.
yourTurn.answer: Hacía frío y llovía cuando salimos del café.
yourTurn.why: The weather is the background; leaving is the event.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Joaquín had already left when Rosa arrived.
yourTurn.answer: Joaquín ya se había ido cuando Rosa llegó.
accept: Cuando Rosa llegó, Joaquín ya se había ido.
yourTurn.why: Leaving came first, so *se había ido*; arriving is the event.

pitfalls.why: Almost. Weather that sets the scene is background, so it takes the imperfect.

pitfalls.right: Cuando llegué, Vale ya había salido.
pitfalls.why: When one thing happened before the other, step back with *había*.

pitfalls.wrong: Estuve leyendo cuando sonó el celular.
pitfalls.right: Estaba leyendo cuando sonó el celular.
pitfalls.why: The action that gets interrupted is background, so use the imperfect.

pitfalls.wrong: Tomás abrió la caja que encontró y vio una carta.
pitfalls.right: Tomás abrió la caja que había encontrado y vio una carta.
pitfalls.why: He found the box before he opened it, so the earlier event takes *había*.

personal: Tell a short story from last weekend in three sentences: one that sets the scene (*Era…* or *Hacía…*), one event, and one thing that had already happened (*Ya había…*).
